Long combos on day one? Not here. 🥊

Boxing, kickboxing, Muay Thai or MMA. Tap any level to change it for today.

Comment TRAIN and I'll DM you the link.

notes: Not approved and not published. The owner approves every post (npm run approve) after seeing the render and every caption.

Facts: Combo Coach opens on your Fight level (own Fight XP in full, Fit at half); YOUR LEVEL marks it; "Easy: Single strikes and short combos. Relaxed pace."; "Advanced: Singles to the hardest combos. Fight pace."; "The higher it is, the longer and harder the combos get"; a picked level is "for today only" (ComboCoachSetup, screenGuides cc-difficulty). The Level page says the top mix "swings from single strikes to the hardest combos" with about half the combos advanced; past level 3 the combos get harder rather than longer (Normal, Hard and Advanced all top out at 6 strikes), so the captions say "longer, then harder" and never "longer and harder" for the whole climb.
The hook footage is the level 1 athlete's own combos (Jab Jab Cross, 4.0 s cadence): the answer to "long combos on day one?". The level 10 combos are the contrast in beat 4.

No number of punches on screen on purpose. The owner's rule is level 1 never gets more than 4 pieces, but the real level 1 pool tops out at 3 (the Level page prints "up to 3-strike combos"), and no combo in the whole pool is longer than 7. So never write "ten-punch combos" (nobody gets one), and say "short" for level 1.
The level 10 clip athlete must be a level 10 FIGHT athlete (Combo Coach reads the Fight side); the cc-lvl10 setup must show ADVANCED with YOUR LEVEL under it.

Footage: each scene's window in the clip is in "timeline". The clips are recorded from the live app by npm run app-broll (needs a built export of the app); after the app changes, re-run it and re-check every window.
